---
title: Usage
subtitle: Folium Typst template guide
description: "Set up and render NBIS reports with the Folium Typst template."
---

## Start a project

Folium requires Quarto 1.8 or later. Create a project from the template:

```bash
quarto use template royfrancis/quarto-typst-folium
```

Use `reports/report.qmd` as the starting point. `reports/demo.qmd` contains examples of supported Quarto and Typst features. `reports/demo-2col.qmd` and `reports/demo-margin-column.qmd` show the two-column and margin-column layouts.

To add the format to an existing project instead, install only the extension:

```bash
quarto add royfrancis/quarto-typst-folium
```

This adds `_extensions/` and nothing else, so there is no `_quarto.yml` to hold the report data. Set `nbis` in the frontmatter of each report.

## Configure the report

Set all NBIS-specific report data in `_quarto.yml`, or in the frontmatter of a report when only the extension is installed. The extension provides no defaults for this key. A report that defines its own `nbis` in its frontmatter overrides the project-level data:

```yaml
nbis:
  id: "0000"
  contributors:
    - name: "Person A"
      email: "name@nbis.se"
      affiliation: "NBIS"
      roles: "NBIS Staff"
    - name: "Person B"
      email: "name@example.com"
      affiliation: "Some university"
      roles: "Principal Investigator"
```

`name` is required. `email` is optional. `affiliation` and `roles` accept either a string or a list. Contributors without a role appear under **Contributor**.

`id` is the support issue number. It appears in the header of every page after the cover. To show it on the cover as well, add it to the subtitle with the `meta` shortcode, as `reports/report.qmd` does.

The cover defaults to class `NBIS REPORT`, the bundled NBIS logo and background, a logo height of `0.8cm`, and a font size of `12pt`. Override only the presentation values you need under `folium`; every omitted value retains its extension default:

```yaml
folium:
  class: "NBIS PROJECT PLAN"
  logo:
    path: assets/logos/custom-logo.svg
  logo-height: 1cm
  font-size: 11pt
  background:
    path: assets/images/custom-bg.png
```

A path is relative to the file that sets it: to the project root in `_quarto.yml`, and to the report in its frontmatter. A report in `reports/` that uses a file from the project's `assets/` folder therefore needs `../assets/logos/custom-logo.svg`.

To leave out the logo or the background image, set it to `false`:

```yaml
folium:
  logo: false
  background: false
```

The extension provides the PDF defaults, including A4 paper, Lato, one column, numbered sections, and report margins. Enable the format in the frontmatter of each report, as `reports/report.qmd` does:

```yaml
format:
  folium-typst: default
```

To make it the default for a whole project, set it under `format` in `_quarto.yml` instead. Every document that does not set its own `format` is then also rendered as a PDF, including website pages such as this guide.

Project or document settings override these defaults. For example:

```yaml
format:
  folium-typst:
    papersize: us-letter
    columns: 2
    number-sections: false
    margin-left: 2cm
    margin-right: 2cm
```

The margins are set with `margin-left`, `margin-right`, `margin-top` and `margin-bottom`, which default to 2.15 cm, 2.15 cm, 3 cm and 3 cm. The cover logo is placed at the left and top margins.

Document frontmatter supplies the report text:

```yaml
---
title: Report title
subtitle: NBIS Support 0000
description: Short project description.
date: last-modified
date-format: "DD MMM YYYY"
---
```

Top-level headings can be written with `#` or `##`. If a document has no `#` headings, Quarto treats `##` as the top level, as the demos do, and numbering still starts at 1.

## Language, numbering and fonts

Set the document language with `lang`, and optionally `region`. The default is English. The language sets hyphenation, quotation marks and generated labels such as figure captions ("Figur 1") and callout titles ("Notera"). The `Contents` heading is the exception; see the next section.

```yaml
lang: sv
region: SE
```

Sections are numbered `1`, `1.1`, `1.1.1` by default. Change the pattern with `section-numbering`, which takes a Typst numbering pattern, or turn numbering off with `number-sections: false`. This pattern numbers the sections `1`, `1.a`, `1.b`, and so on:

```yaml
format:
  folium-typst:
    section-numbering: "1.a"
```

The font is Lato. Use another font with `mainfont`, and add the folder that holds it with `font-paths`. The folder is added to the bundled fonts and does not replace them. It follows the same path rule as above, relative to the project root in `_quarto.yml` and to the report in its frontmatter:

```yaml
format:
  folium-typst:
    mainfont: "Open Sans"
    font-paths: assets/fonts
```

## Contents and columns

The template does not add a contents page automatically. For a contents page, add:

````markdown
```{=typst}
#outline()
#pagebreak()
```
````

The heading is `Contents`, whichever `lang` is set. To change it, pass a title, for example `#outline(title: [Innehåll])`.

For a two-column report, set `columns: 2`. The cover remains one column automatically. Keep the contents page one column with:

````markdown
```{=typst}
#single-column[
  #outline()
  #pagebreak()
]
```
````

See `reports/demo-2col.qmd` for a complete example.

Content can also be placed in a margin column with the `.aside` and `.column-margin` classes. This narrows the main column for the whole document. See `reports/demo-margin-column.qmd` for examples.

## Render

Render one PDF:

```bash
quarto render reports/report.qmd --to folium-typst
```

Render the full project:

```bash
quarto render
```

Output is written to `docs/`. Standard Quarto Markdown features such as citations, cross-references, tables, figures, callouts, and code blocks are supported.
